cards.definition: The research practice of converting unobservable quantities about AI's future — remaining usable training data, deployable agent capacity, the cost of a fixed capability — into bounded forecasts with stated assumptions and uncertainty intervals. Epoch AI is the canonical practitioner: measure physical inputs (data stocks, chip shipments, cost curves), then project the frontier from them.

Villalobos et al. (2024) model both sides of the ledger: data demand, driven by neural scaling laws that tie dataset size to the square root of training compute; and data supply, estimated from Google's index size and Common Crawl's bytes-per-page, converted to tokens. Quality filtering and multi-epoch training adjust the raw stock down and up respectively; Monte Carlo simulation propagates uncertainty.

The paper's Table 1 point estimates (95% CIs where given): Common Crawl ~130T tokens [100T-260T]; indexed web ~510T [130T-2100T]; whole web ~3100T [1900T-5200T]; images ~300T; video ~1350T. The Figure 1 projection: median full-stock utilization in 2028, with datasets approaching ~4e14 tokens and ~5e28 FLOP of training compute for non-overtrained models.

Epoch's October 2026 report (Jason Li) estimates agent capacity as A = E x c: effective hardware supply E (HBM memory shipped 2025-27, in GB300 equivalents) times serving capacity c (concurrent agent sessions per GB300). Closed-model concurrency is inferred from API spending per agent-hour in TraceLab session traces; open-model concurrency comes directly from SemiAnalysis's AgentX serving benchmarks at fixed streaming-speed targets.

Epoch's headline result (2026-10-02): HBM shipped 2025-27 could support roughly 30-170 million concurrent frontier-model agents, or ~1.9 billion sessions of an efficient open model (DeepSeek V4 Pro benchmarks). Pooled hourly rates: ~$16-18/agent-hour on Codex harnesses vs $24-50 on Claude Code. Using only 20% of central capacity implies $2.6-5.3T/year in API-equivalent spending - far above projected developer revenue, so Epoch flags demand, not chips, as the binding unknown.
cards.term: 30-170 million agents - and the demand question

cards.definition: Epoch's September 2026 'plunging price of thought' finding: the cost of a fixed level of benchmark performance has fallen ~47% per quarter (~13x/year) since 2023 - faster than electricity, compute, batteries, or DNA sequencing ever fell. The budget implication: capability priced out today may be affordable within a year, so fixed long-run cost assumptions age quickly.

Two cautionary lessons recur across the corpus. First, estimates decay: the 2022 data-wall projection of ~2024 exhaustion was revised to ~2028 after web data filtered better than assumed. Second, the binding constraint moves: by 2026 the live debate is as much about inference economics and demand (agent capacity vs willingness to pay) as about raw training-data supply. Forecasts are dated artifacts, not constants.

notes: Frontier-core module for IL-23: capability forecasting as a discipline. Two verified primary sources anchor it: the Villalobos et al. Model names and figures are 2026 estimates and will decay - the as_of date is load-bearing. Supplemental slots: IL-12 (inference economics), IL-16 (scaling laws and data constraints).
objectives: Explain Epoch AI's capability-forecasting method: physical inputs (data stocks, chip shipments, cost curves) projected into bounded frontier forecasts
Reconstruct the data-wall argument: scaling-law demand vs. estimated supply, the quality and multi-epoch adjustments, and the 2026-2032 exhaustion window
Reproduce Epoch's agent-capacity estimation (A = E x c) and its key result: ~30-170M concurrent frontier agents from 2025-27 HBM shipments
Interpret inference cost curves (~47%/quarter since 2023) and their budget implications for AI engineering
Apply the decay lesson: why frontier forecasts carry as-of dates and why the binding constraint moves over time

quiz.answer: Frontier capability forecasting: measure physical inputs of AI progress (data stocks, chip shipments, cost curves) and project the frontier from them, reporting assumptions and uncertainty intervals.
quiz.question: What discipline does Epoch AI practice, and what are its raw materials?

quiz.answer: Dataset size should scale roughly with the square root of training compute. As compute compounds, data demand compounds with it - against a finite stock of human-generated text.
quiz.question: How do neural scaling laws (Kaplan 2020; Hoffmann/Chinchilla 2022) create the demand side of the data wall?

quiz.answer: Quality filtering (only a usable fraction of deduplicated web text performs well) shrinks the raw stock; multi-epoch training (repeat passes over the data) stretches the effective stock. Uncertainty is propagated by Monte Carlo simulation.
quiz.question: Name the two adjustments Epoch applies to raw web-token counts, and say which direction each moves the effective stock.

quiz.answer: Median full-stock utilization in 2028 (80%-style interval 2026-2032), at roughly 4e14 tokens of dataset size and ~5e28 FLOP of training compute - one or two years earlier if frontier models are overtrained.
quiz.question: State the data-wall paper's headline forecast (window, median year, scale at exhaustion).

quiz.answer: A = E x c: effective hardware supply (HBM shipped 2025-27, in GB300 equivalents) times serving capacity (concurrent agent sessions per GB300). Closed-model concurrency from API spending per agent-hour (TraceLab traces); open-model concurrency from AgentX serving benchmarks.
quiz.question: Write Epoch's agent-capacity formula and say where each term's numbers come from.

quiz.answer: Using just 20% of central capacity would imply $2.6-5.3T/year in API-equivalent spending, far above ~$1T in projected developer revenue by end-2027. The buildout could produce a capacity glut - whether demand justifies the investment is the key uncertainty.
quiz.question: Why does Epoch conclude that demand, not chips, is the binding unknown for the agent buildout?

quiz.answer: Because the 2022 estimate was revised from ~2024 to ~2028 when web data performed better than assumed, and because by 2026 the binding constraint had moved from training-data supply to inference economics and demand. Every frontier number is a dated artifact.
quiz.question: Give two reasons the module carries as_of dating on every fast-moving claim.
